findings.title: Guard the missing destination before checking its integration
findings.body: When Google Meet is selected and destinationCalendar is null or empty, mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined. Accessing its integration now throws instead of falling back to Cal Video as the previous optional access did. This prevents bookings from being created when the host has no destination calendar.

findings.title: Pass the current destination to non-Google calendar adapters
findings.body: Each host's credential is now used to create an event, but every call receives the entire destinationCalendar array. Office365, Lark, and BaseCalendarService still select only its first entry. For a collective booking, a secondary host therefore tries to create an event in the main host's calendar using their own credentials. Office365 and Lark can reject the request, while CalDAV can filter out every calendar and report success without creating anything. Scope the event's destination to the current host or make all adapters select by credentialId.

findings.title: Keep secondary destinations when the organizer has no calendar
findings.body: The event initializes destinationCalendar to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination. The optional push then silently discards teamDestinationCalendars, even if other collective hosts have connected calendars. Those hosts receive no directly created calendar events. Initialize an empty array and append the secondary hosts' destinations regardless of whether the organizer has one.

findings.title: Preserve credential IDs on video references
findings.body: This assignment now sets credentialId to undefined for every video result, whereas it previously preserved result.credentialId. The cancellation handler only deletes a video meeting when its booking reference has a credentialId. Newly created Zoom and other credential-backed video meetings will consequently remain active after their bookings are cancelled.

findings.title: Preserve destination selection for calendars without a credential ID
findings.body: DestinationCalendar.credentialId is nullable, and EventManager explicitly supports that case by trying credentials of the matching integration. This lookup cannot match such a destination to the supplied credentialId, so creation now falls back to primary instead of using the configured externalId. Existing destinations without a credential association can therefore receive bookings in the wrong calendar.

findings.title: Restore a usable fallback when a reference lacks an external calendar ID
findings.body: This branch runs only when externalCalendarId is absent, but then searches for a destination whose externalId equals that absent value. It cannot select a real destination, so Google updates receive an undefined calendarId and fail. The corresponding delete fallback also searches this way and instead targets primary, potentially leaving the original event behind. Older booking references without externalCalendarId must still be able to use their destination calendar.

findings.title: Reconstruct all collective destinations when confirming a booking
findings.body: Confirmation still constructs destinationCalendar from only the booking's single stored destination or the confirming user's destination. The secondary collective destinations assembled during handleNewBooking are not persisted, and this handler does not reload them. Since pending bookings create their integration events upon confirmation, collective events requiring approval still create an event for only one host. The payment webhook creation paths have the same omission.

findings.title: Cancel recurring events using each reference's credential
findings.body: For cancellation of all remaining recurring bookings, the newly resolved secondary host credential is ignored. The inner loop uses only the booking owner's credentials and selects just the first calendar reference from each occurrence. Although the outer loop now visits every host reference, it repeats the same first-reference deletion rather than deleting secondary hosts' events. All occurrences are marked cancelled while those hosts' calendar events remain active.

findings.title: Do not reverse organization slug creation based on billing
findings.body: The slug condition was reversed from !IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED to IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED. With team billing disabled, a newly created organization now gets neither a slug nor requestedSlug, despite the handler configuring its requested domain. With billing enabled, it publishes the slug immediately rather than retaining it solely as requestedSlug. This unrelated change breaks the existing organization provisioning behavior and should be reverted.
